reason: The bearing frames should support the rotating shaft on the mechanism base.
expectation: The frames will attach to the base, ready to hold the crankshaft.

effect: The bearing frames are installed, so the base should now support the crankshaft.
reason: The crankshaft belongs in the newly fitted shaft bearings.
expectation: The crankshaft will fit into the bearings and be able to rotate.

effect: The crankshaft is installed and can turn, so the cam is the next likely part.
reaction: The assembly is progressing as expected.
reason: The off-centre cam should fit on the turning crankshaft to produce the up-and-down motion.
expectation: The cam will attach to the crankshaft and turn with it.

effect: The cam is installed; its off-centre edge changes height as the shaft turns, ready to move a follower.
reaction: The comparison with a centred disc makes the mechanism clearer.
reason: The follower guide should keep the rod aligned as it moves against the cam.
expectation: The guide will attach to the mechanism, ready to hold the follower rod.

alternatives.reason: The rod might fit directly, but it seems likely to need its guide first.

effect: The guide fits the follower rod first, creating a guided follower ready for the cam mechanism.
reaction: I had the right purpose for the guide but guessed the assembly order incorrectly.
reason: The guided follower should fit against the cam so its changing height can move the rod.
expectation: The guided follower will attach to the mechanism and ride on the cam.

effect: The guided follower is installed above the cam, leaving the spring and crank handle to fit.
reaction: The parts are coming together as expected.
reason: The follower spring should help keep the rod in contact with the cam as it turns.
expectation: The spring will attach to the follower mechanism.

effect: The spring has no available operation yet, so another part likely needs fitting first.
reaction: The fitting order was less obvious than I expected.
reason: The crank handle is the remaining obvious part to attach to the shaft.
expectation: The handle will fit the crankshaft so the cam can be turned.

effect: Turning the crank revealed that the follower sometimes loses contact with the descending cam; the spring now has a clear purpose.
reaction: The test made the need for the spring clearer.
reason: The spring should help the follower stay against the cam.
expectation: The spring will keep the follower in contact as the cam rises and falls.

effect: The spring keeps the follower against the cam, completing the reliable up-and-down motion and the chapter goal.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the failed test lead to a working mechanism.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the crank was most worthwhile: it exposed why the follower needed a spring, making the final fix understandable.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying the spring before testing the crank was a little frustrating because its purpose seemed clear, but it was not available yet.

surprise.text: The follower could hang in its guide and lose contact as the cam descended; I had expected it to follow automatically.

arbitrary.text: The spring being unavailable before the crank test felt somewhat arbitrary, even though the test explained its purpose.

continue.text: Yes. The cam comparison and the follower test made the mechanism understandable, and I would be curious to see how it makes the dragon wave.
